title: About
text:
I am a bioinformatician and computational biologist with a background spanning genomics, epigenetics, scientific software and research computing.
I started in biology and moved into bioinformatics at a time when the field was still establishing itself as such. Over the years, my work has changed from individual data analyses to developing pipelines and software, managing data, working on large collaborative projects, and eventually building and leading a bioinformatics core facility.
I have always been interested in the path from the biological question to the computational solution - understanding the science, working with the data, choosing or developing the right tools, and creating the systems that allow this work to be done reproducibly and sustainably.


My scientific background is in genomics and molecular biology, with a strong focus on epigenomics and gene regulation. I have worked with genomic and epigenomic data across hematopoiesis, leukemia and cancer, as well as other biomedical research areas.
Much of my work has involved DNA methylation, alongside transcriptomics and other functional genomics approaches.



As bioinformatics has evolved, so has my work.
What started with data analysis and computational methods increasingly turned into scientific software, reproducible workflows, data management, HPC environments and research infrastructure.
Leading a bioinformatics core facility made these connections very apparent. Good bioinformatics depends not only on the analysis itself, but also on how data enters a project, how workflows are run, how results are documented, how software and data are maintained, and how scientists and technical teams work together.
As a result, these aspects have become an integral part of how I approach bioinformatics



I am currently extending my background towards machine learning and AI-enabled biomedical research.
My interest is not in AI as a separate discipline, but in how these methods can become useful parts of scientific practice — integrated with biological knowledge, research data, computational workflows and reproducible infrastructure.



I write about some of these ideas in Building Bioinformatics, where I reflect on bioinformatics, software engineering, workflows and research infrastructure.
I am also documenting what I am learning about machine learning and generative AI in Catching up with AI.
For a more structured overview of my work, see Projects, Experience, or my CV.

title: Experience
text:
My work experience spans quite different research environments: from basic and discovery research, through high-throughput genomics at a sequencing centre, to building and leading a bioinformatics core facility within a translational biomedical research institute.




2021–2025



Josep Carreras Leukaemia Research Institute (IJC), Barcelona
I built and led the institute’s bioinformatics core facility, supporting research groups across leukemia, immunology and other biomedical research areas.
My role combined scientific bioinformatics with team leadership and research support, as well as developing the processes, workflows and infrastructure needed to provide a sustainable bioinformatics service.
The work ranged from individual research projects to developing some of the broader bioinformatics environment within the institute, including data management, reproducible workflows, computational infrastructure, training and collaboration with experimental scientists and clinicians.







2013–2019



National Centre for Genomic Analysis (CNAG-CRG), Barcelona
I worked in a sequencing-centre environment on large-scale genomics and epigenomics projects, with a particular focus on DNA methylation and whole-genome bisulfite sequencing.
Much of my work was connected to the BLUEPRINT Epigenome project and the study of DNA methylation during hematopoietic differentiation and in leukemia. I also worked on projects in other biomedical research areas such as Inflammatory Bowels Disease (IBD).
Working at a sequencing centre brought together biological research with the computational challenges of processing large volumes of sequencing data. My work included data analysis, computational methods and the development of pipelines and software, including contributions to gemBS and gemBSR.







2012–2013



RIKEN Omics Science Center, Yokohama
I worked on the computational analysis of transcription and transposable element activity during early zebrafish development, integrating CAGE and ChIP-seq data.




2009–2012



Centre for Genomic Regulation (CRG), Barcelona
I worked on transcriptomics and alternative splicing as part of the ENCODE project, developing and applying computational methods for large-scale RNA-seq analysis.
This included work on GRAPE, a computational pipeline developed for the analysis of RNA-seq data within ENCODE.







PhD · 2008



University of Canterbury, Christchurch, New Zealand
My doctoral research focused on microsatellite evolution, combining molecular biology with computational approaches to study short tandem repeats in yeast.
It was during my PhD that I increasingly moved towards computational biology and bioinformatics.

title: Projects
text:
Selected topics and projects from my work in computational genomics, bioinformatics infrastructure and scientific software. They reflect different parts of my work, from analysing biological data to developing computational tools and connecting them into research workflows.






DNA methylation · eCLIP-seq · RIP-seq · Translational research

Collaborative research investigating mechanisms of gene regulation and potential molecular biomarkers in different biomedical contexts.
The work includes DNA methylation profiling using microarrays, as well as eCLIP-seq and RIP-seq analyses to investigate post-transcriptional regulation through interactions between RNA molecules and RNA-binding proteins.

LHX1 study →
Rett syndrome study →
METTL1 study →





DNA methylation · WGBS · BLUEPRINT · Integrative genomics

Research into DNA methylation and epigenomic regulation during normal hematopoietic differentiation and in leukemia, primarily within the BLUEPRINT project.
The work combined large-scale whole-genome bisulfite sequencing with other genomic and epigenomic data to investigate normal differentiation and disease-associated changes.

Immune-system DNA methylation →
B-cell differentiation methylome →
Multiple myeloma epigenome →










Research infrastructure · Team · Processes · Reproducibility

Building the Bioinformatics Unit at the Josep Carreras Leukaemia Research Institute involved more than establishing an analysis service.
The work included developing working practices for project intake and data management, reproducible analysis workflows, computational infrastructure, documentation and training, while supporting multiple research groups and projects.
It shaped how I think about bioinformatics as an ecosystem connecting people, data, software and infrastructure.




HPC · Data management · Workflow integration · Research computing

Development of an integrated computational environment supporting DNA methylation array analysis, connecting metadata capture, reproducible analysis workflows, HPC computing and the organization of analysis results.
The system brought together BioForms for structured metadata capture, EPipe for reproducible analysis, HPC scheduling and MethylationDB for organizing and accessing DNA methylation data.
Read more in Building Bioinformatics →









DNA methylation arrays · Reproducible workflows · R

Development of a reproducible workflow for processing and analysing Illumina DNA methylation array data.
EPipe was developed within the bioinformatics core facility to standardize frequently requested analyses while retaining the flexibility needed for individual research projects.




Metadata · Data capture · Research workflows

Development of a tool for structured capture of research metadata and project information.
BioForms was designed to make metadata collection part of the research workflow and to provide structured information that could be used by downstream computational processes.




DNA methylation · Data management · Research software

Development of a database for organizing and accessing DNA methylation data and analysis results.
MethylationDB formed part of the wider computational workflow connecting project metadata, analysis pipelines, computing infrastructure and research results.




WGBS · Pipeline development · R

Development of software for processing and analysing whole-genome bisulfite sequencing data.
I contributed to gemBS, a pipeline for high-throughput bisulfite sequencing analysis, and developed gemBSR, an R package for downstream analysis and interaction with gemBS results.
